title: Turnip greens, frozen, cooked, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Turnip greens are the leafy tops of the turnip plant, a nutrient‑dense green vegetable. In this product the greens are blanched, quickly frozen, and later enriched with a small amount of fat to improve flavor and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turnip greens belong to the Brassicaceae family, the same as broccoli, kale and cabbage.
They are an excellent source of vitamins A, C, and K, as well as calcium and iron.
Turnip greens are traditional in Southern U.S. cooking and are also used in Asian stir‑fries.
Rapid freezing after harvest preserves most of the nutrients.
Adding a modest amount of fat helps the body absorb fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone metabolism.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements and gut health.

items.title: Improves mineral absorption
items.content: The added fat enhances the absorption of vitamins A and K.

items.title: Cruciferous vegetable allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to Brassicaceae plants.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Processed frozen greens can contain added salt; check the label if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Oxalate levels
items.content: High oxalate content may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen greens in a skillet with a little oil, stir‑fry them, add to soups or stews, or serve as a side dish with meat or fish. They can also be microwaved for 3‑4 minutes until hot.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product frozen at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, use within 1‑2 days and do not refreeze.
